note.note:
Consult Summary:
- Adult with known history of asthma presenting with 2–3 days of wheeze, cough, shortness of breath and subjective fever; assessed as likely asthma exacerbation; plan to increase bronchodilator use, provide peak flow meter and spacer, start antihistamine and arrange review.

History:
- Presenting complaint: recent wheeze, shortness of breath, cough and reported fever.
- Timeline:
  - Symptoms began 2–3 days ago.
  - Patient reports current limitation on walking to work and difficulty completing sentences on occasion; currently feeling relatively well at time of consult.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - No specific triggers identified by patient during this episode; doctor noted possible triggers (pollen/allergic or viral infection) as differential.
  - Patient previously used inhaler therapy; advised to increase inhaler use now.
- Associated symptoms / systems review:
  - Cough (non-productive; patient reports no phlegm or hemoptysis).
  - No chest pain.
  - No nocturnal wakening.
  - Reduced exercise tolerance; unable to walk to work recently.
  - Reports hay fever and eczema history.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No blood when coughing.
  - No chest pain.
  - No ICU admissions historically for asthma.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma: history since childhood, described as "quite bad" in childhood; required inhaler therapy and occasional hospital attendance for checks. Patient states asthma improved/stopped a few years ago (patient also reports ongoing salbutamol use—conflict noted; see Quality checks).
- Allergic rhinitis (hay fever).
- Eczema.

Medications:
- Salbutamol (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- No other regular medications reported.

Allergies:
- No medication allergies reported.

Social History:
- Lives with partner.
- Occupation: engineer.
- Work: sometimes works from home; has taken sick leave recently due to symptoms.
- Smoking: does not smoke.
- Alcohol: approximately one glass of wine every 2–3 days.
- No recreational drug use mentioned.

Family History:
- No family history documented in the transcript.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals:
  - Patient-reported temperature: "thirty seven" (37°C).
- Examination findings:
  - None documented in the transcript.

Investigations:
- No investigations performed or results reported during this consult.
- Plan to prescribe a peak flow meter for home monitoring.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute asthma exacerbation (likely)
  - Assessment: Patient with known asthma presenting with wheeze, dyspnea, cough; potential triggers include viral infection or pollen/allergic cause per clinician.
  - Plan:
    - Increase use of short-acting bronchodilator (salbutamol) to 2–4 puffs every 4 hours initially (dose/route/frequency documented as discussed; specific inhaler type and dose not otherwise documented).
    - Provide spacer to improve inhaler delivery (doctor to prescribe spacer).
    - Provide inhaler technique support via pharmacist when collecting spacer.
    - Prescribe peak flow meter for home monitoring and advise recording first thing in the morning and in the evening over the next week.
    - Safety net: patient to contact service immediately if fever increases or wheeze worsens.
    - Arrange review in approximately 1 week to reassess and consider additional controller therapy if needed.
- Issue 2: Allergic rhinitis / contributing allergic trigger
  - Assessment: History of hay fever; may be contributing to current exacerbation.
  - Plan:
    - Start a regular oral antihistamine (OTC from pharmacy; clinician offered to add guidance to notes). Specific agent/dose not documented.
- Issue 3: Monitoring and follow-up
  - Plan:
    - Review peak flow readings after one week (phone review planned to discuss values).
    - Pharmacist to demonstrate spacer and peak flow use.
    - Earlier review if symptoms worsen.

General Plan items if applicable:
- Clinician counseling provided regarding likely asthma flare, possible causes, and need for closer monitoring and follow-up.
- No additional medications or investigations completed during the consult beyond planned prescriptions.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but expected elements:
  - Objective vital signs (respiratory rate, heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation) not documented.
  - Formal physical examination findings (lung auscultation) not recorded.
  - Exact inhaler type(s) previously used or currently available not documented.
  - Precise salbutamol dose, route, and frequency prior to and during this episode not documented.
  - No documented spirometry or peak flow baseline values yet.
  - Pregnancy status not documented (if applicable).
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - Patient reports "I have fever" yet reports temperature of 37°C when asked (conflict between subjective fever and measured temperature).
  - Patient states asthma "stopped" a few years ago but also reports ongoing use of salbutamol "normally" over recent years (conflicting statements about current/ongoing inhaler use).
- Transcript quality:
  - Overall conversation audible and understandable; occasional brief inaudible or overlapping words but no major loss of clinical information.
